source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Chandler campus publishes 169 MW of IT capacity across eight buildings, the largest single campus figure mapped in Arizona and the only reason the state's published total reaches 512.02 MW.

The concentration is a disclosure artifact as much as a power fact. Only four of the 57 mapped Arizona facilities publish a megawatt figure at all, so one campus carrying 169 MW dominates a total built from a very small sample. The 2 million square feet of technical space and the eight facility codes PHX1 through PHX8 describe scale, but the operator publishes no address, no postal code, no rack count, and no accelerator count. Converting 169 MW to hardware requires an assumption the data does not supply: at 40 kW per rack it implies roughly 4,225 racks, at 10 kW per rack roughly 16,900, and neither is the operator's claim.

The certifications describe eligible workloads, not occupants. SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2, PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, TIA-942, and Green Globes qualify the campus for financial, payment, health, federal, and telecommunications work, but no tenant is named. A certification is not evidence of a particular tenant.

What this does not cover is the grid side. There is no utility, no interconnection queue position, no power purchase agreement, and no on-site generation in the data, so the 169 MW is a capacity figure rather than a statement about where the electrons come from or whether they have been secured. The campus sits in Chandler, Arizona, and the siting constraints that put it there are not published here.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
